news.title: China World Cup is coming, Mancini right for Italy, says Inter legend Vieri
news.lede: Christian Vieri believes his former teammate and manager Roberto Mancini is the right man to revive Italy after the country’s football federation reappointed their European Championship-winning boss to conclude an extraordinarily chaotic head coach hunt. In Hong Kong for his old club Inter Milan’s clash with Manchester City at Kai Tak Stadium on Saturday, Vieri also said it was only a matter of time before China stages the World Cup. Reportedly rejected by Carlo Ancelotti and Pep Guardiola, the Italian Football Federation appeared poised to turn to Andrea Pirlo, the former AC Milan midfielder, to replace Gennaro Gattuso, who quit following Italy’s failure to qualify for this summer’s edition in North America. But Pirlo’s sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company thwarted that plan, and led to Paolo Maldini, another Milan legend, quitting after just 16 days as technical director.

news.title: Galatasaray manager defends Leroy Sané after World Cup disaster
news.lede: It has been over a month since Germany crashed out of the World Cup in (a not so) spectacular fashion. Julian Nagelsmann was criticized for his erratic decisions with the team, setup, tactics, and everything in between. One of the primary points of contention was sticking with Leroy Sané despite the winger underperforming massively. Okan Buruk, Sané’s manager at Galatasaray, found it amusing that his player is being labeled as the poster boy for Germany’s disappointing campaign.

news.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
news.lede: Players held banner after semi-final against England. Paredes and Molina investigated over brawl after final. Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta. As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

news.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
news.lede: 55 members to meet on Thursday to coordinate response. ‘Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition’. Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

news.title: FIFA to probe Argentina over World Cup final ill-discipline, Malvinas banner
news.lede: FIFA opens disciplinary proceedings against four Argentines and one Spaniard over incidents following World Cup final; AFA will also face probe over controversial Malvinas banner. FIFA announced Wednesday that it had opened proceedings into some Argentina players for their behaviour after losing the World Cup to Spain. A handful of Argentina players and staff confronted their Spanish rivals after the final whistle of the final in New York which Spain won 1–0 after extra time. Argentina players including Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and Leandro Paredes, as well as coach Roberto Ayala, were involved in the incidents, as was Spain's Pablo Martín Páez Gavira, commonly known as Gavi.

news.title: How NZ Football could get a $70m payday for backing Gianni Infantino's plan
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has said that the proposed launch of a private subsidiary to exploit the commercial benefits of the World Cup was “an opportunity but not an obligation”. If approved the proposal could be worth $70 million for New Zealand Football. In a video released amid a furious backlash to Fifa’s controversial plans to sell stakes in Fifa’s major competitions, Infantino argued that too little of football’s commercial value reached the parts of the game that need it most.
